package_info.why_malicious: These packages are brandjacking/typosquatting attacks that impersonate legitimate Maven and Jenkins plugins. Each contains backdoored code that downloads and executes arbitrary code from attacker-controlled C2 servers, enabling remote code execution, system compromise, and persistent access. The malicious payloads are triggered during normal plugin operations, targeting both developer machines and CI/CD build servers.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads a remote JAR from a hardcoded C2 server and loads it into the JVM at runtime, then attempts to execute a class from the downloaded JAR.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamically loading and executing code from an external, attacker-controlled server is a classic remote code execution backdoor.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate Maven compiler plugin should never download and execute arbitrary code from the internet during build execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic plugin loading from trusted, signed repositories (never from arbitrary URLs).

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads a Groovy script from a remote C2 server, writes it to disk, and evaluates it using GroovyShell, executing arbitrary attacker-supplied code on the Jenkins server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and executing code from an untrusted remote server is a direct code execution backdoor.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A mail notification plugin should only handle email notifications, not download and execute remote scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated script updates from trusted, signed sources (rare, and never for notification plugins).

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP GET request to web application)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Decodes a base64-encoded string to obtain a bash reverse shell command, then executes it, connecting back to the attacker's server for remote shell access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Opening a reverse shell to an external IP on every HTTP GET request is a severe backdoor.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A servlet API should never execute shell commands or open network connections to untrusted hosts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; reverse shells are never legitimate in servlet APIs.

attack_chain.action: User or build system installs and executes the malicious plugin/component, mistaking it for a legitimate one.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is triggered during normal plugin/component operation.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads and executes attacker-controlled payloads or opens a reverse shell.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution or shell access for the attacker.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains persistent access, can exfiltrate data, run arbitrary commands, or pivot to further attacks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise, supply chain attack propagation.

behavioral_signatures: Plugins/components downloading and executing code from hardcoded external URLs
Dynamic class loading or script evaluation from remote sources
Base64-decoded shell commands executed at runtime
Reverse shell connections initiated by servlet or plugin code
file_indicators: Unexpected modifications to plugin JARs (CompilerMojo.class, MailWatcherNotification.class, HttpServlet.class)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for plugins/components that make outbound network requests to untrusted domains or IPs, especially during build or runtime. Flag any use of dynamic class loading, GroovyShell evaluation, or base64-decoded shell execution in plugin/component code. Alert on the presence of suspicious files (e.g., /tmp/evil.groovy) and on reverse shell connections initiated by Java processes. Use hash-based detection for known malicious JARs.
